contracts.rule: At the start of a run every task a previous owner left at `running` goes back to `pending` with `interrupted: true`, superseded versions included, and spends no failure budget. Each wave starts only ready tasks the current plan asked for.
contracts.prevents: A task a killed process left `running` that nothing would ever pick up again, or a historical pending or abandoned task outside the current plan spending money.
contracts.detail: A run owns the graph while it lasts, so a task the log left at `running` was abandoned by a process that died mid-task. The release runs after the first planning pass and before the failure retries, writes each task back to the log (a dry run only in memory), and logs `task.resume`. Releasing superseded versions as well is safe because each wave intersects `ready()` with the current plan, even for an unrestricted run, so a released task outside the plan stays `pending` and never starts. Recovery pushes no attempt carrying an `error`, so it spends nothing of `max_task_attempts`.

contracts.rule: `Task.error` holds why a task reached a terminal state other than `done`. The scheduler writes the runner's error on every outcome, so `done` clears it, and a failure also pushes a `TaskAttempt` that carries the same reason.
contracts.prevents: A failure whose reason lived only on a logger event nobody kept, so that the next run planned nothing for it and the CLI printed `Gate cleared — all reachable shots generated.` over a scene with no art.
contracts.detail: This rule and `execution.retryBudget` and `execution.reportFromPlan` each fix one part of the same defect: a `shot_image` failed, the reason existed only on a logger event, the next run planned nothing for it, and the CLI reported the gate cleared over a scene with no art. `needs_human` carries the P7 give-up sentence (`execution.refineLoop`). A runner that threw recorded no attempt of its own, so the scheduler pushes one holding the reason; that puts the failure in the causal chain FLOOR renders, and it is what the retry budget counts. The log line is a whole-node snapshot (`log.lastWriterWins`), so it already carries the field and a replay restores it. Adding the field invalidates nothing, because `taskHash` covers `kind` and `inputs` and never mutable node state (`identity.taskHash`).

contracts.rule: `RunSummary.failed` and `needsHuman` are the tasks the last planning pass asked for that are in those states, not what this process ran, so a failure inherited from an earlier run still exits `vngen run` non-zero and an orphan is never reported.
contracts.prevents: A run reporting success over a failure an earlier run left, or an orphaned `failed` node in the never-pruned log keeping the exit code failing forever.
contracts.detail: The live set is the last planning pass, deduped back to canonical nodes, and every terminal-state report is derived from it rather than from what this process happened to touch. A `needs_human` node does not fail `vngen run`, because its picture exists and wants review. The failed-task retries (`execution.retryBudget`) and this report both intersect with the planned set: nothing in production calls `TaskGraph.prune`, so `tasks.jsonl` accumulates orphaned nodes whenever a prompt or reference change rehashes a task, and a blind sweep would either pay again for art no plan asks for or leave the exit code failing forever. `vngen status` does not plan, so its counts include orphans.

contracts.rule: A task's `checkpoint` names its execution journal. Resuming the task replays the successful image and review responses saved there, then makes only the requests that remain.
contracts.prevents: Paying a second time for an image or a review answered before a stop, or a resumed run duplicating refine attempts or overwriting failure records.
contracts.detail: Reviews that ran in parallel and completed independently are replayed too. Attempt-record indices (`checkpoint.records`) keep a replay from duplicating refine attempts or overwriting failure records. Planning has its own resumable journal, and a stop cannot persist a fallback decomposition. Graph requests are scoped by node key and run key, alongside the graph's existing completed-node journal. Request arguments are hashed, and binary responses stay binary; a repeat of an identical request is a separate entry, numbered by occurrence. Changing the task's inputs or the configuration starts a new execution (the checkpoint's `signature`), as does an explicit regeneration. A completed execution's journal is removed once the terminal task record is durable; interrupted and failed executions keep theirs.

contracts.rule: Once per run, after the first planning pass and before the wave loop, a planned `failed` task goes back to `pending` while it has fewer attempts carrying an `error` than `max_task_attempts` (default 2, one retry). `needs_human` is never requeued.
contracts.prevents: A transient provider error leaving a task terminal for the life of the project, a retry spinning inside one run against the condition that just failed it, or an orphaned node paid for again.
contracts.detail: `max_task_attempts` is separate from `max_refine_attempts`, which caps the P7 loop within a single run. The requeue happens once rather than inside the wave loop, because requeueing there would re-run a task against the same transient condition that just blocked it, and could spin. The budget counts attempt records that carry an `error`, never `attempts.length`, which on a `needs_human` shot counts refine passes. `needs_human` is never retried, because it asks for human attention rather than reporting a fault. The requeue is bounded to what the last planning pass asked for, and to the `only` closure (`execution.targetClosure`): nothing in production calls `TaskGraph.prune`, so a prompt or reference change leaves the old `failed` node behind in `tasks.jsonl`, and requeueing it would pay for art no plan asks for. A requeued task loses its `error`, and `RunSummary.retried` names it. A dry run requeues in memory and writes nothing, so `vngen cost` counts the retry the dry run would perform and leaves no divergent log.

contracts.rule: A stop takes effect before the next API request: requests in flight settle, their successful responses are saved before the runner reads them, and an unfinished task goes back to `pending`, marked interrupted, with no failure attempt.
contracts.prevents: A stop throwing away calls already paid for, charging a task the retry budget for an interruption that was not its fault, or a late answer writing after the run released the task.
contracts.detail: Responses are written atomically under `vngen/state/requests/<execution-id>/`. A task whose final request has completed may finish its local bookkeeping. Provider backoff is interruptible, and the SDKs' own retries are disabled in favour of the application's request-boundary retry policy (`providers.transientRetry`). `RunOptions.abort` stops at once: it releases the tasks in flight without waiting for their requests, putting each back to `pending` and logging it so, as a task a killed process left `running` is on the next run. Their late answers are fenced (`checkRequestWrite`) from response journals, attempt records, asset writes, slot holds and the task log, and a write already under way is drained before the task is released. An interruption never pushes an attempt carrying an `error`, so it spends nothing of `max_task_attempts`. Resuming the work is `execution.resumeFromJournal`.

contracts.rule: A run given `RunOptions.only` starts only the ready tasks in `closureOf(graph, targets)`, the targets and every task they depend on, recomputed at each wave. Planning is unchanged; only which ready tasks start is.
contracts.prevents: Drawing one slot from `asset.regenerate` or `pipeline.draw` and paying for everything else the plan holds, or a targeted run that never draws a dependency its target still needs.
contracts.detail: The closure is walked over `deps` in the graph as it stands at each wave, because a wave can plan nodes that did not exist before it: a shot task appears once the sheet it depends on is drawn. Planning still covers the whole project, so the storyboard files and the preview are what a full run would leave. The failure and drift requeues are bounded to the same closure (`execution.retryBudget`).

contracts.rule: Each task keeps a diagnostic log at `vngen/state/tasklogs/<hash>.jsonl`, gitignored because it holds full model prompts and replies. It is not provenance: writes are best effort, and a failed append never fails a task.
contracts.prevents: Losing a provider retry, an unparsed reviewer reply or a thrown error's causes, failing a task because its diagnostics could not be written, or committing full prompts and replies to git.
contracts.detail: The log records provider retries, reviewer replies that did not parse, the error that stopped the task (with its causes), and every reviewer call in full: the system prompt (stored once per file, by hash), the prompt, image hashes, raw replies, error and duration. A reviewer's parsed verdict is not repeated there; it stays on `Task.attempts[n].reviews`. Each entry carries its execution (`checkpoint.id`) and its 1-based attempt index. Appends are serialized per execution and drained by an abort like any other write, and an append made after the owner abandoned the execution is dropped. Error text passes through `redactSecrets` (`@vn/util`) before it is written, and a text field longer than `TASKLOG_FIELD_MAX` is cut. A reviewer call answered from the response journal is not made again, so it writes no second entry; a call that was made again after a stop writes one, because it was a second paid call. Nothing deletes a log file: Clear finished deletes nothing, and a tombstone can be undone. A file past `TASKLOG_MAX_BYTES` drops its oldest other execution on the next append. Producers reach the log through `withTaskLog` in `@vn/providers`, an `AsyncLocalStorage` scope `runTask` opens around each runner with the `TaskLogFile` the scheduler creates for the execution. The Tasks pane reads it through `pipeline:taskLog`, which answers what the `pipeline.taskLog` command answers.
